solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Onset of obesity on monkeys leads to complaint in pavilion

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of obesity
titis are small South American monkeys

explanation.surface: An overweight cricketer's monkey business ends with someone feeling ill in the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: The pavilion here is not a cricket clubhouse but the pinna, the outer flap of the ear, a dictionary sense the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is inflammation of the ear, and the pavilion is an old anatomical name for the outer ear.

clue.text: Head off from one Siberian city for another

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: Tomsk is a city in western Siberia

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off from one Siberian city to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Tomsk and the answer are cities in Siberia, so 'another' carries the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-west Siberia, a second Siberian city beside Tomsk.

clue.text: Take up drink after getting ragged in violent storms

parts.note: ragged clothes are torn

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up reads it from the bottom upward

parts.note: soda is a drink

explanation.surface: A sailor drinks to recover after being battered by a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornados are violent whirling windstorms, a variant plural spelling of tornadoes.

clue.text: Leaves writer inside to get liquor

indicators.note: something inside another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: tea is made from leaves
a quill is a pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: An author goes inside to fetch a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing, but means tea leaves; 'writer' is the pen, not the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequilla is a variant spelling of tequila, the Mexican spirit distilled from agave.

clue.text: Royal house for all to see in shoot

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: to shoot or start is to move suddenly
U is the film certificate for a universal audience

explanation.surface: A royal family's shooting party is open to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England, a royal house.

clue.text: Neat enclosure good for Charlie, more than a handful for Angus

definitions.text: more than a handful for Angus

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means the second is swapped out and the first put in its place

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat enclosure is a pen for cows
G is the usual abbreviation for good
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A tidy cattle pen is praised, while a Scotsman finds something too much to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle. Angus stands for any Scot: gowpen is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gowpen is the Scots measure of two hands cupped together, a double handful, so more than one handful.

clue.text: Rattle's double bass interrupting wind

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into the middle of it

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
B for bass, doubled

explanation.surface: Conductor Simon Rattle's double bass section breaks into the wind players.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattle looks like the conductor Sir Simon Rattle, but it is the verb meaning to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle on is to chatter quickly and thoughtlessly, which is what gabbling means.

clue.text: Nameless public official brings seal

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation for name is taken away

parts.note: a notary public is an official who certifies documents

explanation.surface: An anonymous official applies a seal to a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' suggests a notary's stamp but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An otary is an eared seal, such as a sea lion or fur seal.

clue.text: Adroit tips rubbished, one does feel a heel

indicators.note: something rubbished is torn apart, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's clever advice is dismissed, and they feel like a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feel a heel' sounds like feeling ashamed, but a foot doctor literally handles heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A podiatrist treats feet, so examining a patient's heel by touch is routine work.

clue.text: Vikings seem excited with goddess coming round

indicators.note: something coming round another wraps around it
excited letters are stirred up out of order

parts.note: the letters of seem, rearranged
a Norn is one of the three Norse goddesses of fate

explanation.surface: Viking raiders look thrilled as a goddess appears among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen are the medieval Scandinavians whose seafaring raiders are known as Vikings.

clue.text: Spy HQ, one's almost distraught with it being attacked

definitions.note: a cryptic second definition: a mole's station

indicators.note: a distraught person is in turmoil, so these words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at the spies' headquarters is nearly frantic about an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two routes: 'Spy HQ' builds MOLE (spy) plus STATION (HQ), and ONE ALMOST IT rearranges into the same letters; 'being attacked' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Molestation is the act of harassing or assaulting someone, the state of being attacked.

clue.text: Forget about colonialist waffling — it's balls!

indicators.note: waffling talk is muddled, so the letters come out jumbled
to forget something is to leave it out

parts.note: a is a dictionary abbreviation for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a colonialist's rambling talk as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's balls!' reads as British slang for nonsense; here balls are formal dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotillion is a formal ball or the elaborate dance performed at one.

clue.text: Indian officer's subordinate had abused army regulation

indicators.note: abused letters are mistreated and knocked out of their order

parts.note: a sub is a subordinate
the letters of had, rearranged
AR is the abbreviation for army regulation

explanation.surface: An officer's junior has mistreated soldiers against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A subahdar was the chief Indian officer of a company of sepoys in British India.

clue.text: Flog duck by the sound of it in Barnsley

indicators.text: by the sound of it in Barnsley
indicators.note: we are told to listen to the word as a Yorkshire speaker would say it

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, and nothing in Yorkshire dialect is nowt

explanation.surface: Someone whips a duck that has a Yorkshire accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnsley is a town in Yorkshire, where 'nowt' means nothing; in cricket a duck is a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout is a Russian leather whip, and as a verb it means to whip someone with one.

clue.text: Feathers of hawk and wading bird found in rubbish

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: BS, short for bullshit, means rubbish or nonsense
a rail is a marsh bird of the crake family

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher finds plumage from a hawk and a wader dumped in the trash.
explanation.definitionFit: Brails are the thigh feathers of a hawk, in the language of falconry.

clue.text: More affable Master of the Rolls receives a bow

indicators.note: one who receives something takes it inside

parts.note: MR is the abbreviation for the judge called Master of the Rolls
taken as written
a bow is a knotted tie

explanation.surface: A senior judge becomes friendlier after someone bows to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like a gesture of respect but is a bow tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey means friendly and sociable, so its comparative is a synonym for more affable.

clue.text: Ridicule a lapse in conversation — one puts one's foot in it

definitions.text: one puts one's foot in it

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the result is heard rather than read

parts.note: ridicule is mock, a stays as written, and a lapse is a sin

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a slip of the tongue, the classic case of putting your foot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts one's foot in it' is the idiom for a gaffe, which matches the surface; literally, a shoe has a foot put in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather shoe, something a wearer literally slides a foot into.

clue.text: Book on reporter not the first one to cause litigation

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is left off

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a narrator reports events

explanation.surface: A book about a journalist who is not top of the field leads to a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrator is someone who habitually stirs up lawsuits and quarrels, a vexatious litigant.

clue.text: Case laid out for plant

indicators.note: laid out means spread out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal case is set out for someone placed as a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be an informant in a legal case, but it is the garden kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidalcea is a genus of flowering plants of the mallow family, known as prairie mallow.

clue.text: Latin term, one for the ultimate of precision in reproduction

definitions.text: Latin term, one for the ultimate of precision in reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction remakes something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
one thing standing for another takes its place in the word

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: 'the ultimate of' keeps only the last letter of 'precision'

parts.note: the last letter of precision, the one to be replaced

explanation.surface: A Latin phrase describing exact copying, letter by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the N of LATIN TERM for I, then rearrange. The whole clue also defines the answer: it is a Latin term meaning reproduced with full precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Literatim is Latin for letter for letter, describing a copy made with total precision.

clue.text: Black hole, apparently small in surrounding band

indicators.note: the band is said to surround the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a collar is a band round the neck
AP is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
S is the usual abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A black hole looks tiny inside a ring of light around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently small' reads as a description of the hole, but the two words are separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsar is a star that has collapsed under its own gravity, an older name for a black hole.

clue.text: Sound of alarms for old spouses

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is heard, not spelt

parts.note: alarms are frights or fears

explanation.surface: Wedded couples of old are startled by the noise of alarm bells.
explanation.walkthrough: Pheere is a Spenserian word, so the definition carries 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheere is an archaic word for a companion or mate, including a husband or wife.

clue.text: Go to crack school parole as before

indicators.note: cracking something opens it so another thing can be put inside

parts.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school
go and pee are both informal words for urinating

explanation.surface: A prisoner sets out to break into a school while released on parole.
explanation.walkthrough: Parole looks like early release from prison, but its older sense is word of mouth or speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In its obsolete sense parole meant spoken words or talk, so it is a former synonym of speech.

clue.text: Iced tea on the rocks? Reject it and porter

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked, so the letters are broken up
to reject something is to throw it out of the group

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to be thrown out

explanation.surface: A hotel porter turns down an iced tea served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' means served with ice, but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadee is an old variant of caddie, an errand boy or porter who carries things.

clue.text: Pressure on Nigerian ready to return fine marble

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the naira is Nigeria's currency, and ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on a Nigerian who is prepared to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not prepared but ready money, cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Parian is a fine white marble quarried on the Greek island of Paros, prized by sculptors.

clue.text: Saudi term of abuse could be "swine"

indicators.note: the letters could be other words if put in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a term is an end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of abuse

explanation.surface: An insult in Saudi Arabia might be calling someone a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term of abuse' reads as an insult, but a term is an end, giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Suidae is the zoological family name of pigs, hogs and boars.

clue.text: Some overseas left-handers for the Ashes

indicators.note: only some of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some left-handed batsmen from abroad are picked for the Ashes cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, but here the words just mean ashes from a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Easle is a Scots word, used by Burns, for hot cinders or embers.

clue.text: Old nobleman rising needs both hands with grandchild

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right hands
oe is a Scots word for grandchild

explanation.surface: An aged aristocrat getting up needs two hands and a grandchild's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Eorl is the Old English word for a nobleman, the ancestor of earl.

clue.text: Feet opened somehow in two seconds

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits in between the other letters
done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of opened, rearranged
S is the abbreviation for second, twice

explanation.surface: Someone's feet were opened up in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' here means metrical feet in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical foot of two long syllables, so spondees are poetic feet.

clue.text: What can keep engine from overheating? Nitre possibly, can

definitions.text: What can keep engine from overheating?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters

parts.note: the letters of nitre, rearranged
can and cooler are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A puzzled motorist wonders whether saltpetre in a can might stop an engine overheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' sits as a verb in the question, but at the end it is the noun for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercooler is a heat exchanger that cools air between compression stages in a turbocharged engine.

clue.text: Name for maiden schoolgirls in Brownies

indicators.note: one letter standing for another is swapped in to replace it

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
misses are girls, especially schoolgirls

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls in the Brownies swap names when their leader marries.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies looks like the junior Girl Guides, matching the schoolgirls, but means household goblins.
explanation.definitionFit: A nis is a friendly household goblin of Scandinavian folklore, much like a Scottish brownie.

clue.text: Pictures in lobby mostly showing industrial action

indicators.note: something in another thing sits inside it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lobby is an entrance hall
pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: Paintings hung in a foyer depict a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hartal is a stoppage of work and business in India, used as a political protest, a kind of strike.
